We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (alkene). 3) sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline (or aniline with extra N?). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: amide bond between carbonyl (from unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline with NH). So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid: /C=C/C(=O) (attached to aromatic ring). Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring via double bond: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the acid part is the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Wait the sulfonamide attaches to phenyl ring (first ring) via NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl ring which has the unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus retrosynthesis: Step 1: break amide: get α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step 2: the α,β-unsaturated acid derived from Doebner modification of aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) with malonic acid. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (p-methyl phenyl? Actually the ring is c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. The aldehyde would be same aromatic ring with CHO substituent at position where the side chain attaches. So we need aromatic aldehyde: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (with methyl on other ring? The methyl is on first phenyl ring attached to sulfonamide). The aldehyde is attached to sulfonyl phenyl? Wait the sulfonyl phenyl is the second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). It has the side chain at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So sulfonamide attached to phenyl (c2). That phenyl has side chain at para position (maybe). So the aldehyde precursor would be same phenyl with CHO at that position, and sulfonyl group attached? The sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via N-SO2- to the first phenyl ring. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl with sulfonamide? Actually sulfonamide formation is step 3: amine (first phenyl with methyl) reacts with sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the sulfonyl chloride attached to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) with sulfonyl chloride group (SO2Cl). So step 3: sulfonamide formation between aniline (first phenyl with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So we need to identify the two precursors: 1) methyl aniline (p-toluidine) Cc1ccc(N)cc1. 2) aryl sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. That sulfonyl chloride has the unsaturated amide side chain attached already. So step 2: that side chain is formed via Doebner modification from aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid, giving α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl. Then step 1: amide formation between that acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Wait the aniline for amide is the aniline attached to the unsaturated acid side chain (c3ccccc3N). That's a separate aniline (anilide). So we have two aniline fragments: one is the methyl aniline (p-toluidine) that forms sulfonamide; the other is aniline that forms amide with the unsaturated acid. So overall three steps:

- Step A (retro): break amide: gives α,β-unsaturated acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). (Amide formation forward)
- Step B (retro): break double bond formation: α,β-unsaturated acid derived from aromatic aldehyde (aryl-CHO) via Doebner modification with malonic acid (gives unsaturated acid). So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). (Doebner forward)
- Step C (retro): sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) reacts with p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) to give sulfonamide. So precursor: p-toluidine and aryl sulfonyl chloride (which already contains the unsaturated acid side chain). The aryl sulfonyl chloride is derived from step B product after conversion of acid to sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonyl chloride is derived from the same phenyl ring as the unsaturated acid side chain, but with SO2Cl instead of SO2NH-? Wait the sulfonyl chloride attaches to the first phenyl ring via N. In target, the sulfonamide is between first phenyl (with methyl) and sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the second phenyl with sulfonyl chloride group (SO2Cl) attached, and also the unsaturated acid side chain attached to that phenyl. So we need to generate that sulfonyl chloride from the unsaturated acid? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is separate functional group; we could imagine that the sulfonyl chloride is commercially available or can be made from the corresponding sulfonic acid via chlorination. But for retrosynthesis we can just treat it as a building block.

Thus final route: target -> (retro step 3) sulfonamide disconnection -> p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (which contains unsaturated acid). Then (retro step 1) amide disconnection on the aryl sulfonyl chloride: break amide to give α,β-unsaturated acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then (retro step 2) Doebner modification: break unsaturated acid to aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid.

Thus we need to provide JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We can search for templates matching these transformations.

First, amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Search for functional_groups_broken aliphatic carboxylic acid, formed amide. Already we have templates 133246 etc. Use that template ID (reaction_id). The tool returns reaction_id but we need template_id. The template_id likely same as reaction_id? In examples they use template_id numeric. We'll use the reaction_id as template_id.

From earlier result, template for amide formation: reaction_id 133246, template_hash etc. So template_id = 133246.

Second, Doebner modification: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. Need template. Search for functional_groups_broken aldehydes, formed C-C double bonds and aliphatic carboxylic acid. Not found earlier. Maybe there is a template for Knoevenagel condensation (aldehyde + malonic acid). Let's search for functional_groups_broken ["aldehydes"] and formed ["C-C double bonds","aliphatic carboxylic acid"] again but maybe need to include "carboxylic acids". Already did, got none. Could try functional_groups_formed ["C-C double bonds"] only.
